plt.grid(True)

# Load the CSV file into a DataFrame

daily_temp_change = df.groupby('city')['temp_c'].diff().reset_index()
cumulative_precipitation = df.groupby('city')['precip_mm'].cumsum()

# Plot the derived series over date in aligned panels with zero reference lines, endpoint labels, and a shared legend

# Plot daily temperature change

# Plot cumulative precipitation
plt.plot(daily_temp_change['date'], cumulative_precipitation['precip_mm'], label='Cumulative Precipitation')

# Add labels and title
plt.xlabel('Date')
plt.ylabel('Temperature (C)')
plt.title('Daily Temperature Change and Cumulative Precipitation')

# Add legend
plt.legend()

# Show the plot
plt.show()

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the CSV file
data = pd.read_csv('/mnt/uploads/sales.csv')

# Group by 'region' and calculate the sum of 'revenue' and 'orders'
grouped_data = data.groupby('region').agg({'revenue': 'sum', 'orders': 'sum'})

# Plot the grouped data
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(grouped_data.index, grouped_data['revenue'], label='Revenue')
plt.plot(grouped_data.index, grouped_data['orders'], label='Orders')
plt.legend()
plt.show()

# Calculate the residuals for each group
residuals = grouped_data['revenue'] - grouped_data['orders']

# Plot the residuals
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(residuals.index, residuals, label='Residuals')
plt.legend()
plt.show()

# Find the point with the largest residual
largest_residual_index = residuals.idxmax()
largest_residual_value = residuals.loc[largest_residual_index]

print(f"The largest residual value was {largest_residual_value:.2f} for region {largest_residual_index}.")
```

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the CSV file into a DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv('/mnt/uploads/weather.csv')

# Create a function to plot the data
def plot_weather(df):
    # Extract the date, city, temperature, rainfall, and air quality
    date = df['date']
    city = df['city']
    temp_c = df['temp_c']
    precip_mm = df['precip_mm']
    aqi = df['aqi']
    
    # Plot the temperature, rainfall, and air quality
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    ax.plot(date, temp_c, label='Temperature (C)')
    ax.plot(date, precip_mm, label='Precipitation (mm)')
    ax.plot(date, aqi, label='Air Quality')
    
    # Add labels and title
    ax.set_xlabel('Date')
    ax.set_ylabel('Value')
    ax.set_title('Weather Data')
    
    # Add legend
    ax.legend()
    
    # Show the plot
    plt.show()

# Call the function to plot the weather data
plot_weather(df)
```

# Load the CSV file into a DataFrame

# Create a 2x2 grid of subplots
fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(10, 10))

# Plot the revenue area chart
axs[0, 0].plot(df['month'], df['revenue'], color=colors[0], label='Revenue Area')
axs[0, 0].set_title('Revenue Area Chart')
axs[0, 0].set_xlabel('Month')
axs[0, 0].set_ylabel('Revenue')

axs[0, 1].set_title('Orders by Region')
axs[0, 1].set_xlabel('Region')
axs[0, 1].set_ylabel('Orders')

# Plot the revenue-versus-orders bubble scatter colored by region
axs[1, 0].scatter(df['month'], df['revenue'], c=df['region'], cmap='viridis', s=50, label='Revenue vs Orders')
axs[1, 0].set_title('Revenue vs Orders Bubble Scatter')
axs[1, 0].set_xlabel('Month')
axs[1, 0].set_ylabel('Revenue')

# Add a peak month annotation
axs[1, 0].annotate('Peak Month', xy=(1, 0.9), ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=12)

# Set the background color to dark
